name: Primary shapes
summary: The circle, the square and the triangle in flat colour, used as the whole picture or as a sign.
how: Use 1 to 3 shapes at large size; let one shape fill 30% to 60% of the frame.
Fill each shape with one flat colour; no gradient and no outline.
Put the shapes on a plain ground with 30% or more empty space.

origin.note: Kazimir Malevich shows the Black Square and other pure shapes at the 0,10 exhibition.

adoptions.via: Wassily Kandinsky asks Bauhaus students to match the circle, the square and the triangle to blue, red and yellow.
Malevich and his pupils build a teapot and cups from blocks and cylinders at the State Porcelain Factory.
Designers at the Berlin and Halle porcelain works build services from the circle, the cylinder and the flat disc.
Yusaku Kamekura puts one red circle over gold type on the poster for the Tokyo 1964 Olympic Games.
Memphis Milano sets circles, triangles and squiggles on furniture and prints in loud colour.
